Round 3 (30-40mins): (Completely Finance Based) 
1.​ It was an online round in which a guy from Europe joined in. 
2.​ I was given a case/situation:​
Suppose there were only 2 markets (China & US) for trading in the whole 
world and one commodity is being traded in both the markets at the same 
price and in China market supply is lower than demand and in the US 
market supply is higher than demand. 
3.​ So, do you think Trade should happen between these two markets if the 
price of commodities is same in both markets? 
4.​ At what price differential, do you think the trade between the market will 
start? 
5.​ So, what do you think will happen in future, will this trend continue, the 
price of commodities change or not? 
6.​ What will be your investing strategy and at what level of risk you will pull 
out of the trade?
Jahnavi Kalisetty 
 
QRT checks your thought process and your ability to apply concepts to solve 
problems rather than the concepts per se and it’s a holistic evaluation

Round 1: (About 40mins) 
14 people got shortlisted and 3 were waitlisted (They took interview of all 17 
people) 
Personality Based: 
1.​ About my intro, I have background of UPSC, so questions based on that 
2.​ I changed company after working for a year, so he asked about that (There 
might be profile-based questions, to check your personality, so if your 
profile has any hiccups like frequent company changes or UPSC prep, be 
thorough about what you’re going to answer)
Technical: 
1.​ Trading strategies, Mean Reverting and Pairs trading. And out of all the 
universe of stocks you have how do you select pairs (here they were looking 
for strategy). And follow up questions on these because I said I’ll choose 
pairs based on covariance and cointegration, what is cointegration. In the 
pair of stocks with increasing variance do you think covariance works to 
find out pairs. So there cointegration helps. (Interviewer was directing me 
to think in the direction of co integration by giving hints, It was more of a 
discussion than question and answer based and 90% of my interview is on 
these trading strategies and applying concepts of time series and basics like 
variance-covariance to these strategies) 
2.​ Can you name few statistical tests which you know of 
3.​ Of the tests you mentioned can you think of any test which you can apply 
for the above mean reversion strategy to check the significance of the mean 
reverting signal 
4.​ Difference between

R2 
5.​ Methods to address overfitting 
6.​ Difference between ridge and lasso and when will you use which one 
7.​ What is Type1 and Typer 2 error 
8.​ What is stationarity and ADF test 
9.​ I would like to invest in the FMCG sector, let’s say in HUL at some point of 
time in the near future, how should my strategy be? (Here they were 
looking for signals) 
Most of the discussion was on trading strategies and how we can apply our 
knowledge of statistics to validate our signals/hypothesis

Quite unconventional round, they gave me a problem statement and expected me 
to solve it, and they were open for discussion, you can think out loud and tell 
them what strategies you are thinking of and if they have any different strategy in

repeating pattern in your time series data, how do you check that (This is not 
cyclicity and they won’t come in cycles or seasons, just at a random point of time 
there was a pattern repetition)

rounds.content:
Round 3: (About 20-25 mins) 
(Two panels, one for Energy and one for Metals) 
This is more of a cultural fit

round 
1.​ Tell me about yourself 
2.​ Why QRT 
3.​ Why did you join PGDBA after working as senior data scientist 
4.​ What were your day-to-day activities in your last job as senior data 
scientist 
5.​ Tell me about any project you have worked on, as a Data Scientist 
6.​ Were you alone in doing this project or you worked in a team and what’s 
your role in that team 
7.​ Tell me about your city (This was common question for almost all of us in 
that panel) 
8.​ Tell me about your family, Hobbies 
9.​ Tell me about organic farming (hobby). Try to keep interesting hobbies so 
that they get curious about it
Suggestions: 
1.​ Practice coding basic, pandas and python although we (Batch 10) didn’t 
have DSA in our test, we never know what QRT tests on for your batch. So, 
start practicing DSA too. And don’t use chatgpt for everything, you’ll be 
doing lot of projects in KGP, get hands on esp., in EDA and fitting simple 
models 
2.​ Try to do FRM project something relating to trading strategies which will 
help you in knowing and understanding those strategies better, whether 
you keep them in your resume or not as knowing them helps in Hedge 
Fund companies 
3.​ Finance is important, know about derivatives and what are the different 
instruments in derivatives, and which one do you use in which situation, 
mostly application of the things that you know of.  
4.​ FRM and CRF are important if you are targeting Quant companies. SAAPM 
is important if you want in depth understanding of Time series and which 
is necessary for Quant companies. For better understanding of Regression, 
Econometrics can be audited or can be taken as elective 
5.​ Try to develop mathematical understanding of regression from RTSM in 
IIT KGP and application oriented from SAAPM and Econometrics
Reeshav Samanta

Round-1 (Face to face interview) 
1.​ Introduce yourself (talked about my work-ex at Aditya Birla Group, 
Hindalco) 
2.​ Explain in detail about the role – talked about my role in Smelter Cast 
House. 
3.​ Explain the end-to-end value chain of Aluminium – told the journey of 
Bauxite in mines to Alumina to Al in Smelter to Cast House then to 
downstream. 
4.​ Asked me to explain the products of Alu. Answered the downstream 
products & their uses. He asked if I can explain the Smelter in detail – all 
the parts like Carbon, Cast House, Potline, did so.  
5.​ Who is the biggest Alu. producer in the world & India – answered Rio 
Tinto Alco & Vedanta Aluminium (by volume) & Hindalco Industries Ltd. 
(by diversity of products)  
6.​ Is India a net exporter or net importer of Alu. – answered net importer – 
he asked why do I feel so – as I felt India still depends on Middle Eastern 
smelters for high grade Alu. 
7.​ Asked me to explain my time-series project – It was on IP of electricity in 
US – he asked if I knew the meaning of IP (Industrial Prod. Index) & where
is that used – I answered but was not clear – then I continued explaining 
the time series project & approach taken. 
8.​ Asked if I can answer some questions on Business Analytics – I said yes – 
He asked what is stationarity – answered  
9.​ Why is log-transformation used? I tried to explain through the lens of 
regression & time-series but he asked me to keep it simple – answered. 
10.​Asked a puzzle - 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/aptitude/measuring-6l-water-4l-9l-bucket
s/ (Partially answered – tried but unable to recall the exact solution) 
11.​On which indices Alu. Is traded – knew about LME, told that. 
12.​How would you predict the yield of a bauxite mine – I first couldn’t get the 
exact question as I thought it’s an un-commissioned mine  – later the 
interviewer re-framed the question to which I tried answering like using 
drill reports, weather data, soil content, last year’s yield.

rounds.round_name: Round-3 (Online interview with Senior Research Director)
rounds.content:
Round-3 (Online interview with Senior Research Director) 
Directly asked me a question. 
Suppose there are two countries in this world – US & China – US has a surplus of 
commodities inventory & Chn with a deficit. How would you create a trading 
strategy if you have this situation? 
This was a tricky question where I had to frame a question to myself. I explained 
by saying about the supply demand curve in both places – Prices going up in 
China while down in the US. First explained imp arb – buying physical inventory 
in the US & selling in China. However, he said a financial trader won’t do so. 
(Obviously!!) 
He asked me to think deeper in terms of Futures. I said something related to that. 
He asked how the situation is if there are two exchanges v/s single exchange. 
Hinted me to arbitrages. Asked how I would think about the dynamics of 
production in both the countries. 
In between he asked me if I did my bachelors in Economics to which I denied. He 
asked if I studied Eco. in my post grad, to which I explained to him that my 
majors are in Business Analytics. 
Finally, he asked as an analyst what all way I can model this situation – I spoke 
about Currency Exchange, Import Export volumes. He hinted me to think about 
import tariffs & CIF (freight charges etc.) 
He asked me if I had any question – Asked him how much he likes the 
multinational global culture at QRT. He was kind enough to answer it. 
Tips: 
1.​ Ask for time in case you have to think for a question. Helps you to frame 
your answer. 
2.​ Seek clarification before answering if you have doubt with the question.
3.​ In general, it’s better to answer a question in case you have little knowledge 
about that, but also giving a disclaimer: “Allow me to make a guess. I feel 
so because….” 
 
Soham Mittal

and why would it have been better?

disease (like model 1 for cancer, and model 2 for HIV), can we use the same 
metrics to evaluate the performance of the model? If yes/no, why?

you handle the consequences of this kind of mistake in the model? How do 
you think about the cost (impact) of giving a false positive result? How will 
that cost be incorporated into the model’s decision-making?

Kshitish Raj  
 
1.​ Why did you leave Deloitte?Why did you take up a sales role after Deloitte? 
He framed and defended that the sales role involved technical and 
analytical challenges  
2.​ How would you increase revenue for Sun Pharma? 
         He had briefly seen on the internet about sun pharma, he had seen that in 
some aspects they were in 10th position, so he framed his answer corresponding 
to that aspect because there is room for development. He also discussed customer 
and market segmentation that can help in generating more profit.  
 
3.​ What do you dislike about the PGDBA program? 
He said having to shift from hostel to hostel even within the same institute.  
4.​ How would you use data science to solve this problem?
​
He said , this is not really a data science problem as the solution is likely to 
involve some solution which is not dependent on finding deep patterns in data. 
Interviewers still pushed for data science framing.  
 
5.​ Do you have any questions for us? 
He said yes, how is Sun pharma handling the impact of Trump's tariff on 
India? They had a discussion on this, and this seemed to have impressed 
interviewers. 
Harsha pabbaraju 
1.​ Many questions about roles and responsibilities in work experience 
2.​ Picked a project he had done for a company he had worked before ( 
analytics project) and went deep into that project details about his 
contribution  
3.​ Why did you switch from chemical engineering  
Anupam das 
1.​ Introduce yourself. 
2.​ My previous work experience was at ZS I explained what I did. 
3.​ The interview went on a different tangent from there. They started 
questioning me about US speciality generics market 
4.​ What is the business model of PBMs? 
5.​ Differences between Indian and Us pharma market 
6.​ This wasn't very technical; they didn't ask anything regarding my projects
Prashant bisht  
1.​ They mostly asked about the workex. There was no difficulty in answering 
the technical part because they know nothing about ML. Project related 
they will ask, 1-2 questions. Easy level. 
2.​ If you have mentioned anything like you did a savings of some lakhs, 
increased efficiency by some % in CV, they will ask how did you reach these 
numbers. They will discuss the numbers in detail. 
3.​ Mostly it’s about the fit and vibe, if they like you, they take you. They will 
keep the interview very interactive, you will not feel any pressure.  
 
Case comps: Not that much. But good to have 2-3 case comps in your CV. 
Winning case comps gives you confidence and that helps. Sunpharma asks to give 
an excel sheet of students with casecomps they have won and POR for shortlist. 
How well you know them is for sure important, but topics should be like you have 
solved some business problem, not just build a model on kaggle dataset. And 
there should be variety in topics. 
 
 
 
Sai kiran 
Sun Pharma- one round experience based, one round resume based- Projects & 
tasks

rounds.content:
Prashant Bisht 
 
PF selected us based on our CV. What I felt based on the people selected for the 
interview, they have 2 projects in common. 1 classification(Finance fraud/loan 
default) and other RAG projects. I had both of them in my CV. There were 2 
panels. Each panel had 2 persons. One asked related to LLM’s and RAG. And 
others asked about traditional ML related to classification. 
 
Since there are 2 teams in PF one is the credit risk modelling team, so 
classification. And others are the GenAI team, LLM and RAG. 
 
1st interviewer:   
1. Explain how the pre-training is done in BERT?  He was expecting “masked 
language modelling” and “next sentence prediction”. Then counter question: 
2. How BERT does classification? He was expecting BERT architecture. CLS 
token, probability distribution over entire vocabulary using softmax. He asked 
BERT since I had mentioned BERT multiple times in my CV.  
3. What is SVD? How is it used in the recommendation model? Since I had a 
project on movie recommendation using SVD. Prepare the meaning of each 
matrix also. A = U sigma V(transpose). What is U, V and sigma?  
4. Explain your RAG project.  
5. Asked about the RAG architecture and the highlighted terms of CV in RAG 
project, like type of retriever I used like MMR. Why this retriever you used. What 
if 5. The query is ambiguous then which retriever to use.  
This was a complete technical interview, all questions asked were CV based. 
 
The 2nd interviewer asked about the ML questions.  
1. The model is performing well on the training set but not on the test set. Why?

rounds.content:
Test round 
Test is just after ppt - on laptop - in offline mode (invigilated and proctored). There were 2 
coding questions and other MCQs that were related to Statistics - probability, hypothesis 
testing - Chi square test, KS test, T-test, ML - regularisation, , . Coding Questions - DSA - 1st 
question was based on a 2 pointer approach. 2nd Question - no idea (refer Atharva / 
Madhur, Nikunj).   (12 people cleared this round) 
Interview

Round 1 
12 students got shortlisted. The 1st round was based on intro, CV - projects, Regression 
assumptions, puzzle - how to cut cake into 8 equal pieces in 3 cuts. Question related to 
properties of normal distribution, skewness - mean median mode in right skewed distribution. 
Then they asked me to think of some unconventional way to get signals to invest in the 
market. Studentised vs standardised residuals. Why QRT.  duration - 30-40 min. 
Interview

Round 2 
Interviewer was from Europe (online) (Emmanuel) . 1st he asked for my intro and 
background.  It was a strategy-based case. Given price data of oil(crude) and gasoline, how 
can we make a trading strategy? What factors to look into. He was leading the case and was 
giving hints. Discussions were on topics like pair trading, heading the position, etc. At the 
end, he asked a question, given 2 portfolios with 0 sharpe ratio and other with 1 sharpe ratio, 
how to combine both to improve sharpe ratio. Then he linked this with the given case. This 
round went for a

round 40 min, and 
Interview

Round 3. 
For this round, only 4 people got shortlisted. Different interviewer from Europe (online) 
(Robin). He first introduced himself. He was head of commodity investment. Then he 
explained about the role a little bit. Then he asked me about my background and why I am 
interested in this role. Then the discussion went on one of my projects which was on portfolio 
optimization. I explained our approach, but he was not satisfied, and he asked why we didn't 
use the optimization route and closed form solution. From thereon, it went a little 
mathematical, and he was asking questions on the density of a set of invertible matrices,
which I didn't have any idea of, but he wanted to have a discussion on that. This discussion 
didn't go well for me. 
 
Soham's Interview Experience

rounds.content:
Round 1 (~30 min) 
1.​ You have 12 balls, 11 identical, and one odd (heavier or lighter). You can use a 
weighing balance three times. Determine the odd ball and whether it’s heavier or 
lighter. 
2.​ For your petrol price time series project, if you had access to any data, what 
exogenous variables would you use, and why? 
3.​ What is the area covered by three standard deviations of the normal distribution? 
4.​ How would you handle skewness in your data? 
5.​ Name a statistical test to detect a leverage point in regression. Are leverage points 
and outliers the same? How would you treat them? 
6.​ What is the difference between SVM and the maximum margin classifier? 
7.​ In your classification project, you handled multicollinearity by regressing one highly 
correlated feature on another and using the residual. Might this cause bias? What 
alternatives could you use? 
8.​ If you have two models—one complex with good validation metrics and another 
simple but with worse metrics—which would you choose and why? 
9.​ What is the PMF of the Poisson distribution? 
10.​In a decision tree, at what level does the splitting occur? What criteria would you use 
to split nodes? 
Peehoo Jain

Round 3 (AMA Region Head) 
1.​ Introduction: 
○​ Discussed a project close to the heart: Drug-Drug Interaction (data sourced 
from Drug Bank). 
○​ Problem: Patients taking drugs for chronic diseases → next drug for different 
diseases. 
2.​ Technical Questions: 
○​ Features used in the project. 
○​ Model used: ANN. Why not XGBoost? 
○​ Ensuring model performance and handling data drift. 
○​ Monetization strategies and managing structural data changes. 
3.​ HR Questions:
○​ Conflict resolution. 
○​ Managing strict deadlines. 
○​ Accountability when a model fails. 
○​ Motivating someone to act against their will (structured CAR framework: 
Context, Actions, Results). 
4.​ Behavioral Questions: 
○​ Explaining technical concepts in simple terms. 
○​ Leadership skills and documentation ability. 
○​ Judged on communication and framing thoughts rather than deep technical 
skills. 
 
 
Muskan Agarwal 
 
P & G :  
 
Pre-Round: 
●​ Online Psychometric Test (MCQ Format)​
 
○​ Includes ethical questions, digit challenges, ratings, and pattern challenges.​
 
○​ Tip: Watch YouTube videos on P&G Assessment Test for better preparation.​
 
●​ CV + Test-Based Shortlisting​
 
1st Round:

Technical Round 
●​ Introduction​
 
●​ Discussion on my project using XGBoost​
 
○​ Detailed questions on XGBoost and its advantages over other ML algorithms.​
 
●​ Few questions on:​
 
○​ Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in Python​
 
○​ SQL​
 
●​ Tip:​
○​ Present answers in a structured way.​
 
○​ Review all past projects thoroughly.​
 
2nd Round: HR / Ethical Round 
●​ Power BI Discussion (since I used it in my previous job)​
 
○​ Asked about advantages and disadvantages of Power BI.​
 
●​ Behavioral Questions using the C-A-R format:​
 
○​ C (Context), A (Action), R (Result) framework for structured responses.​
 
○​ Example:​
 
■​ What revolutionary step did you take in your last job, and what did you 
learn?​
 
■​ What benefits did you gain from PGDBA?​
 
■​ How will you contribute to P&G? Why should we hire you?​
 
 
3rd Round: Case Study & Discussion 
●​ Difference between a Data Scientist and a Data Engineer​
 
○​ In-depth discussion on roles and responsibilities.​
 
○​ Asked how I would resolve conflicts between them as a Chief IT Officer.​
 
●​ Case Study:​
 
○​ Scenario:​
 
■​ As Chief IT Officer of P&G, my team developed a sales forecasting 
model for a new shampoo launch in Dharavi, Mumbai.​
 
■​ A competitor also launched a similar product simultaneously.​
 
■​ Due to this competition, the sales team is failing to meet the 
forecasted sales targets.​
■​ The sales team requests the removal of the model as they believe it is 
inaccurate.​
 
○​ Question: What will you do?​
 
○​ Tip:​
 
■​ Ask detailed clarifying questions before answering.​
 
■​ Consider as many factors as possible in your response.​
 
 
Overall Tips for P&G Interviews: 
●​ Research P&G thoroughly:​
 
○​ Understand the company’s mission, vision, product categories, and net worth.​
 
●​ Practice structured responses using the C-A-R framework.​
 
●​ Be prepared for both technical and behavioral questions.​
 
●​ Think critically in case study discussions.

Includes ethical questions, digit challenges, ratings, and pattern challenges.​
Tip: Watch YouTube videos on P&G Assessment Test for better preparation.

1st introduction. Then he took my credit card default project. Asked objective and how 
exactly I did that. Why F beta score, etc. Then he gave me a scenario that I am working in a 
bank and have access to all this data. How will I approach the same project? How will I 
collect data and how will I merge them, how will I define the business metric etc. 
Then he gave me a scenario, wherein I have to find fraud in the ecommerce business. But 
this is a fresh project - so you have to define fraud, tell the approach to collect the data, and 
how to validate it. Caveat is that it has not been done before. Lots of cross questioning 
happened in this case 
Then he asked me some technical questions from my CV (the keywords) and in general. 
Like when to choose a neural net and when to go for Logistic regression, etc..

rounds.content:
Round 2 - 
It was sort of a leadership round and compatibility check round. It happened with senior 
leadership. They explained my vision of Games24, and asked me what I understood about 
Games and why I wanted to join it. Why I am fascinated about the product. Then they asked 
me if I would prefer updating myself on cutting edge AI ML stuff or just learn that which is 
being required by the current project. They were asking questions to understand if I will take 
initiatives, etc. Then he asked, let's say you deployed a model, but its not working and you 
are not getting results, i.e. business metrics are not showing success. What will be your 
approach and how will you handle that? 
Then he asked if I had any questions - and then we interacted for some time. 
 
RAHUL SINGH 
 
Screening – Test was taken, case study asked, ML ques asked, some basic coding ques 
asked 
Interview- 
How would u rate yourself in Python. I said 6, he said why?
Then in Sql, I said 8​
in Stat & ML, I said 9 
Then he started asking ques on stat & ML 
What is statistics? 
20 mins discussion was on the order of things we use in statistics. Like 1st define Null hyp, 
define significance level, define effect size, decide sample size, methods of collecting the 
sample, find test statistics, comparing with population 
If you have whole population, do you need statistics? 
What is P-value, be crisp on definition.. don’t mention to forgot in last, under the null 
hypothesis is true. 
Ques on confusion matrix. 
The interview went till 45 minutes. 
TIPS- Prepare case studies especially related to Wallet Loading, Customer Retention, etc. 
 
MANIKYAM

something like this.

(that I am part of the team). 
Any questions for us. 
 
Soham

Round 1: Case Presentation (~30 min) 
Case: NYC Hourly Cab Demand Index Forecasting 
●​ Approach: Used SARIMAX (aggregation) + Random Forest Regression 
(disaggregation) to forecast demand indices with dual seasonality (daily and weekly). 
Exogenous variables included subway ridership, precipitation, and temperature. 
1.​ What kind of variable is 'hour of the day' (nominal categorical)? What about the 
demand index (discrete/count data)? 
2.​ How would you statistically measure the association between a nominal variable and 
a count variable? 
3.​ Why did you aggregate data daily instead of weekly? 
4.​ How would you incorporate subway ridership into a forecast when future data isn’t 
available? 
5.​ Would lag 2 for subway ridership show a similar pattern? Why or why not? 
Difficulty Level: Moderate

Round 1 (20 mins) 
Introduction 
What is Bagging? What is Boosting? What is Generalization error? What is Bias – Variance 
trade off? 
When will you use Bagging? When will you use Boosting? 
Ans – Bagging is used When the objective is to use reduce variance, Boosting is used when 
the objective is to reduce Bias. This is a very theoretical answer and it depends on the 
situation and gave a detailed answer. 
They gave me a scenario – If you need to predict a default which is a binary variable 
whether a customer will default or not? Which models you are going to use and why? 
Ans – 3 models – Logistic regression (Linear models), Tree based models, Neural Networks 
Which one will you use and why? 
Ans - I answered I will reject the Neural networks because it is not explainable and also 
reject the logistic regression for its linearity. So, I will go ahead with the Tree Based models. 
Have you worked on Light GBM or any gradient boosting machines? 
From HR, 
If you are given a situation to handle conflict, how do you handle it? 
Ans – I clarified from them who are Stake holders involved and about the situation in detail, 
then I said that I will first talk with all the stake holders involved, ask their opinions and based 
on that I will take the decision which is for the greater good of the organization.

Puzzle: Camel and Banana Puzzle 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-15-camel-and-banana-puzzle/ 
 
A person has 3000 bananas and a camel. The person wants to transport the maximum 
number of bananas to a destination which is 1000 KMs away, using only the camel as a 
mode of transportation. The camel cannot carry more than 1000 bananas at a time and eats 
a banana every km it travels. What is the maximum number of bananas that can be 
transferred to the destination using only camel (no other mode of transportation is allowed). 
 
Approached by incrementally increasing drop point 
Later found that it's already solved in GFG 
 
Puzzle: Tapered circular Rod of some length need to find the midpoint, we can burn the rod 
from any end 
Burn from both the ends simultaneously 
Assumption: Rod consumption is directly proportional to volume 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Himanshu Singh

especially in departments where business knowledge is crucial.

a background from IIT or NIT.

departments require candidates with operational understanding to manage business-related 
challenges effectively.

especially in departments where business knowledge is crucial.

Introduction: The interview began with your introduction. 
 
CV Review: The interviewers went through each line of your CV, asking for details about 
your academic journey, choice of PGDBA, and why you pursued Mechanical Engineering. 
 
Project Deep Dive: They showed particular interest in your time series project, Gen AI 
project, and LLM-based project. Expect in-depth questions about these projects. 
 
CFA: You were asked why you pursued the CFA certification and how it added value to your 
profile. 
 
Linear Regression: The interview briefly covered the assumptions of linear regression, and 
then the focus shifted back to your projects. Most of the interview revolved around 
discussing your project work.

particularly your projects and the operations background you bring. The first round is highly 
technical, while the second round leans towards personal and cultural fit.

-TMAY 
-Which is your favorite project?

-Interview asked questions in depth like what kind of activation functions you used? Why is it

used ReLU activation. 
He has also asked me the calculations for forward propagation and backward propagation?

is the advantage of using ReLU over sigmoid?

gradient. And also when you are calculating the derivative of activation function in 
backpropagation, ReLU is a simple function to calculate the derivative and calculation 
becomes faster and epochs can be performed faster.

algorithm from scratch. Interviewer asked me about What all algorithms I used. I answered 
K-means (Top down) and C-linkage (Bottom-up clustering algorithm). Interviewer seemed to 
have no idea about C-linkage clustering. So, he asked to explain the C-linkage clustering 
algorithm?

English  it consists of antonyms, synonyms, active passive , odd one out , RC passage , 
inference questions like CAT. Overall it consists of the syllabus of CAT and SNAP  but the 
level of difficulty is low .​
​
 Make Sure you  need to clear sectional cut off of each  subject only.​
​
 Interview​
 There were multiple panels. One panel is easy only asking basic  ML questions but mine 
panel was a bit more oriented toward statistics. Luckily I was the only guy who was not 
asked any statistical question.​
 There  were 2 people in my panel, one had proficiency in statistics and the other was HR . 
Both are senior people.​
​
 Interview question 
1- ​ Case Study : Suppose you are playing a rummy circle and you need to find a person who 
is winning the game not because of bias. 
2- ​ Assumption Linear regression 
3- ​ What is multicollinearity 
4- ​ What’s the problem in multicollinearity 
5- ​ Suppose you have 3 columns C1,C2 and C3 . C1 consists of 1,2,3,4. C2 consists of 
1,4,9,16 and C3 consists of 1,8,27,64.  Is there multicollinearity present in it?​
 This question is very basic if you are not able to answer it. Make Sure you work on 
basics.​
 I was not able to answer that. Later when the interview corrected me I got the answers  
correctly. 
6- ​ What is Rank , How will check multicollinearity by rank. ( interview asked me to google it 
and find the answer and still I wasn’t able to do it. 
7- ​ Till this time the situation was already tense. 
8- ​ Then he asked me about Live project Classification , then SVM , assumption of SVM ,​
 pros and cons on SVM . 
9- ​ He asked me about my favorite subject. I do not want to say math, statistics or any  
management subject. That’s why I said clustering   even though it is not a subject  but I 
was very confident about it.​
​
 
10-  Case study – Suppose  there  are 2  people  A and B  belonging to country A and 
country B  respectively. Find the  minimum distance between A and B. Don’t think of 
euclidean distance.​
 Think from the perspective of  Clustering. There is a concept of soft clustering and hard 
clustering  is going to be used.​
​
 
HR question:​
 1 Why did you join PGDBA? Why PGDBA?​
 2 What's the difference between  PGDBA and other b-schools?​
 3 what IIM Calcutta has taught you. (Be specific in your answer) . It was the only 
question, which I was  given with full confidence.  Your answer should be very simple to 
understand.​
​
 
4  Why L&T , what do you expect from  us ? 
  
Finally converted​
 Be thorough with the answer. Make your  answer very simple  to deliver.   Be  prepared 
for HR questions. Most companies reject  students in the HR round only .​
​
 Never Lose Hope !​

rounds.content:
HR Round was kind of a psychometric interview where there were rapid fire questions and they were checking 
whether you are honest. Also they checked your stability and how motivated are you to join the company ?
Courses & Skills Suggested
Arjun Gupta
In my interview, CDS and DBMS were the highlights but it was the combined knowledge gained in various courses that 
played the role in hindsight. I'll briefly share my thoughts about the courses in each semester.
Courses & Skills Suggested
Arjun Gupta
In my interview, CDS and DBMS were the highlights but it was the combined knowledge gained in various courses that 
played the role in hindsight. I'll briefly share my thoughts about the courses in each semester.
ISI lays down the foundation. Inference, DBMS, CDS are very important, for the learnings here would make your journey 
smoother. **Get your hands on coding during this semester**
During IIT semester, make your machine learning concepts stronger. I found FADML, Time Series, DSL Lab, Supply Chain 
Analytics really useful.
The courses at IIM are really important because they give you a perceptive of how to use the knowledge you acquire in the 
last one year to the real world problems. Selected Aspects of Predictive Modelling, Pricing Revenue and Optimization, 
Strategic Management were really useful.
Apart from the curriculum that, I believe, everyone has to follow religiously, I will list down 4 things that I feel are
paramount.
1) Code. Start coding, even if you don't like it. You'll do fine after a year of regular coding. A lot of companies have coding
tests as a way to shortlist candidates.
2)Your resume. Start working on your resume right now. Companies shortlist basis your resume. Participate in competitions,
hackathons. For the interview, you should be thorough with each and every work that your write in your resume.
3) Confidence: I feel the key to crack interviews, apart from your technical knowledge, is confidence. Making interview as a
discussion/ interaction than a very formal interview helped me.
4) Complacency: Stop being complacent, if you are. PGDBA bubble is growing fast, make sure it doesn't burst.
Shubhank Bhanda
a) Inference, 
b) FDBMS (SQL), 
c) IR for NLP & Programming (R & Python)
d) CDS (Machine Learning Algorithms), 
e) Cases and Guesstimates
f)    IIT - Information Retrieval
g)   IIM - Courses which requires solving cases
h) Be through with all the points in your CV and be confident.
i)  Programming is the basic requirement and companies assume we all are good at it so try to master at least one of the
programming language (R or Python).
j)  Try to focus on business application 
Abhi Jain
Prepare your Resume thoroughly. Focus on the "Why" question for everything - why this technique, why not some other 
technique, why this evaluation metric, etc
Deepanshi Seth
a) Database management
b) CV is very important. Be thorough with whatever you have written
c) Both the interviews were more of a conversation. They were checking how clear we are with respect to what we want
to do in life. So consistency in answers is very important as they asked same questions in different forms.
Namit Agarwal
a) Technical - Full understanding of all points mentioned in your CV,
b) Clear Understanding of the projects in PGDBA and in work
c) HR - Self Awareness 
d) Amazon tests you on their 14 Leadership Principles and see if you are a cultural fit
e) CDS, DBMS, Inference, RTSM, FADML, Strategic Management
f) Maintain your CG. Also do as many projects or competitions as you can.
Siddharth Das
a) Time series, CDS, Practical scenario based Competitions, Spontaneity
b) Predictive Modelling(IIM), CDS(ISI),Project management(IIM)
Sambeet Tiady
Apart from course work these definitely helped
a) Deep Learning (Andrew Ng)
b) Questions were asked on simple syntaxes in R and python.
c) Computation for Data Science
d) Inference
e) Prepare CV and projects well. Focus on machine learning and statistics. 
Everything else is secondary for revision. Follow a structure when asked to explain projects.
Korah T Malayil
a) CDS (ISI)
b) FADML (IIT)
c) All Projects
d) Machine Learning Theory
e) Programming skill
f) Inference (ISI)
g) Predictive Modelling (IIM)

You'll gain a better understanding of the nuances of the techniques by this.

Strategic Management were really useful.
Apart from the curriculum that, I believe, everyone has to follow religiously, I will list down 4 things that I feel are
paramount.
1) Code. Start coding, even if you don't like it. You'll do fine after a year of regular coding. A lot of companies have coding
tests as a way to shortlist candidates.
2)Your resume. Start working on your resume right now. Companies shortlist basis your resume. Participate in competitions,
hackathons. For the interview, you should be thorough with each and every work that your write in your resume.
3) Confidence: I feel the key to crack interviews, apart from your technical knowledge, is confidence. Making interview as a
discussion/ interaction than a very formal interview helped me.
4) Complacency: Stop being complacent, if you are. PGDBA bubble is growing fast, make sure it doesn't burst.

rounds.content:
HR Round Questions
a) Is it necessary to use word2vec to train an LSTM?
b) Mention any clustering algorithm? explain k-means clustering?
c) Why pgdba? 
d) What did you do in workex? 
e) Why myntra?
f) The project that you like the most? What was the data? What was the business case/impact? What are the techniques
used?
g) What was your job experience and Have you worked on regression in your job ?
h) Asked about linear regression?
i) Hypothesis testing
J) Feature selection and how to validate and check for the best fit.
k) Application of one of my project (related to image classification) and some concepts of recommendation system?
l) Mostly technical questions on projects. (Korah T.)
m) How would you change your approach if you know certain independent variables with only some level of certainty?
n) (Abhishek Gupta) Interviewed by Pricing and Optimization Guys  
o) CASE: How will you sort the on the basis of profits generated from different catalogue ?
o)1. Then asked which algorithm will  you use ?
p) Questions based on Recommendation Algorithms
q)Explain K means? How will you optimise it? How will you choose the value of k?
r) Explain other clustering algorithm and which one is better among them and why?
s) Explain the objective of one of your project and what is it's business impact.
t) Suppose you have customer data of 1.5 million users and there are 100 advertisements. You have the data 
about which customer has clicked on which ad. A new user joins the platform, you have his data, how will you 
find out which ads to show to him?
u) Suppose you have developed a new cross-sell tool. How will you confirm that it is performing well? 
(Answer: A/B Testing)
v) Describe your work ex. 
w) What was the best project you did in your work ex? 
x) What do you like in linear algebra? 
x)1.Show how you get the matrix expression of least squares estimate? 
x)2.First define what the rank of a matrix is and then what happens if the matrix is not full rank? 
y) How do you handle multicollinearity? 
y)1.Do you always remove variables with high VIF?
y)2. Give 2 scenarios where you should not remove variables because it is part of the design of the 
model (ans: when there are interaction terms in the model, in case of categorical variables) 
Courses & Skills Suggested
a) CDS, FADML and DSL, PRO
b) IR, Gaussian Mixture models, Clustering, DBMS
Suggestion
Positioning is the single most important thing 
1. Your resume should reflect what kind of a role you are seeking. If you want a tech role (data science), position your 
resume in that way with deep learning projects, data science competitions etc. If you want a business analyst 
consulting or finance - position yourself accordingly.
2. Attending company PPTs is a key to cracking interviews - In the PPTs, you get to know what kind of a person the 
company is looking for. Once you attend the PPTs, you can use that knowledge in positioning yourself according to their 
expectations/requirements during the interview. By being a Placecomm, I was compelled to attend almost all the PPTs 
which was a blessing in disguise.
3. During the interview, take every opportunity to stress on how you are the most suitable candidate for the role. In 
Myntra interview, I was asked about my interest in photography (photography contests I had won) and I took that 
opportunity to explain how deep learning could replace DSLR cameras altogether in future.
4. Have multiple "dream companies" and not hold on to just one - this would reduce anxiety during the interview.
5. Push the placecomms to bring the roles/companies that you want to get into.
6. Be thorough with projects and whatever is mentioned in resume in detail.

about which customer has clicked on which ad. A new user joins the platform, you have his data, how will you 
find out which ads to show to him?
u) Suppose you have developed a new cross-sell tool. How will you confirm that it is performing well? 
(Answer: A/B Testing)
v) Describe your work ex. 
w) What was the best project you did in your work ex? 
x) What do you like in linear algebra? 
x)1.Show how you get the matrix expression of least squares estimate? 
x)2.First define what the rank of a matrix is and then what happens if the matrix is not full rank? 
y) How do you handle multicollinearity? 
y)1.Do you always remove variables with high VIF?
y)2. Give 2 scenarios where you should not remove variables because it is part of the design of the 
model (ans: when there are interaction terms in the model, in case of categorical variables) 
Courses & Skills Suggested
a) CDS, FADML and DSL, PRO
b) IR, Gaussian Mixture models, Clustering, DBMS
Suggestion
Positioning is the single most important thing 
1. Your resume should reflect what kind of a role you are seeking. If you want a tech role (data science), position your 
resume in that way with deep learning projects, data science competitions etc. If you want a business analyst 
consulting or finance - position yourself accordingly.
2. Attending company PPTs is a key to cracking interviews - In the PPTs, you get to know what kind of a person the 
company is looking for. Once you attend the PPTs, you can use that knowledge in positioning yourself according to their 
expectations/requirements during the interview. By being a Placecomm, I was compelled to attend almost all the PPTs 
which was a blessing in disguise.
3. During the interview, take every opportunity to stress on how you are the most suitable candidate for the role. In 
Myntra interview, I was asked about my interest in photography (photography contests I had won) and I took that 
opportunity to explain how deep learning could replace DSLR cameras altogether in future.
4. Have multiple "dream companies" and not hold on to just one - this would reduce anxiety during the interview.
5. Push the placecomms to bring the roles/companies that you want to get into.
6. Be thorough with projects and whatever is mentioned in resume in detail.

a) Expectations of company and candidate.
b) Why BNP Paribas for me? looking for managerial capabilities who can build and lead AI Labs team in Mumbai
similar to the lines of Singapore, Paris & NY for BNP Paribas. Challenges, regulatory constraints, deadlines, timeline,
resources, long term commitments etc.

a) Machine learning Models with Business Application that can bring measurable value to the organization .
b) CDS, RTSM, Predictive Modelling, Stochastic Processes, Inference (electives are company specific)
Roles Offered  : a) Business analyst
Job Description :
The Gig: Business Analytics Intern
Flipkart is making eCommerce happen in India. Flipkart’s vision is to make analytics part of its overarching competitive 
strategy, and push it up to decision makers at every level. The Analytics Team serves data driven decision
making along with a diverse set of customers – from Business Teams to Supply Chain Teams to Product Teams. An Analyst is 
expected to grasp the underlying business/ product needs of these teams and develop reports/ analyses/ models that 
solves problems of those respective areas/ functions.
Do you have the passion to analyze data and impact the business materially through what you observe?
What this Job Entails?
Being part of Central Analytics Organization at Flipkart, you get an opportunity to work on diverse set of problems that cut 
across Marketing, Consumer as well as Seller Facing Products on Web & Mobile, Pricing, Customer, various Business 
Categories, end-to-end Supply Chain, Customer Support/ Call
Centre and so on...At Flipkart, high focus on Impact and Ownership allows for freedom to each to experiment and
innovate. The pride is when you see the impact of what you have created. The ability to see what your contribution does to 
the business is a rare experience, add to that the fact that the impact of it is felt by your friends and family in India - the 
experience is extremely gratifying.
You’re Part:
You will work closely with internal Flipkart Teams to identify, define, collect, and track key business metrics for products or 
business process. Conduct business analysis (prescriptive and/or predictive), build reports, dashboards and metrics to 
monitor the performance. Work with the stakeholders to take data driven decisions.
Internship Stipend Offer : INR 1,00,000/- + 2200/- Food Card per month
Shortlist Steps : a) Resume shortlist
b)Technical interview
Duration : 15 minutes.

Round 1 (Online Round)
Walk us through you resume and explain a project that you think we would be interested in knowing 
about,  I chose my project on detecting causal impact using bayesian structural time series. There 
were a couple of follow up questions on it like explain your forecasting methodology, how do you 
evaluate a time series model.
The next set of questions was based on my project on Time series forecasting using Hidden Markov 
models, they asked me to explain how HMM works and how do we interpret the latent states in an 
HMM. They also picked up a project that I had done on building a regression model for Final score 
forecasting in an ODI match. Questions asked were like how does your model take into account the 
recent change in the scoring trends in ODIs. They also asked me how I would model the given problem 
using markov chains.
The final segment of the interview was on a puzzle where you had to find out the fastest 3 horses 
amongst 9 horses using 3 a racing track with three lanes in the minimum number of races. 
Continued on next slide…

6
Final Interview (In person Round)
They explained the roles on offer and asked for my preference. They asked why I think I would be a 
good fit for the role and whether I had interacted with any seniors at the firm. There was a very easy 
puzzle on data imputation after that.
HR Question: What role would you prefer?
Additional Information
My interview luckily happened to be fairly technical but most other interviews had a very dominant 
case component where people were given a fictitious data set and had to come up with ways to 
generate revenue for DE Shaw. Resume based questions would mostly be on regression and time 
series projects. You should be well versed with your fundamentals and must be able to clearly explain 
the techniques used. Also, keep your CGPA as high as possible.

Final Interview (In person Round)
It started with any questions I had for them. I asked some questions about the roles offered and it 
went on for about 15 minutes. 
Then I was asked this guesstimate question: How many people fly in and out of Kolkata in any time 
frame of your choice? They gave me a few minutes to think, helped me out a lot and nudged me in the 
right direction throughout. I think they were just checking whether I could pick up their clues. This 
went on for another 15 minutes and then the interview concluded.
HR Questions: None
Additional Information

explaining projects, focus on the business aspects, dataset, and your learning and keep the technical 
stuff on the lower side unless you're asked specific questions on it. Try to follow their hints when 
you're missing something.

like KNN based and regression based imputation. They also gave another time series toy dataset and 
asked me to decompose that series that into it's trend and seasonal components. There was no error 
term involved and hence it was more or less straightforward.

lot in the interview.

Questions based on work experience - asked to describe the project and then

Basic questions based on Linear Regression:
-When do you use regression model with constant term and without constant term - give practical 
examples. 
-What is the significance of constant term. 
-Let’s say you fit two regression lines with same data - one with constant and one without constant. Are 
the coefficients same in both the cases. If not, are there any cases when they will the same.

One puzzle (with 5-6 seconds limit per answer):

offered. Then one case and then questions based on regression were asked. 
1)
Case: Post 2008-09 in USA, the oil consumption had started declining till 2014. What could be the 
reason. (Post Financial crisis it was a growth phase, everyone would expect that oil consumption in 
the country should go up, but it was going down.)

Regression based question: Questions based on difference between leverage point and outlier. Gave 
multiple cases to identify which point would have more impact on the regression line.

Since I was in Placecomm, I was asked about the experience, how it affected the preparation etc.

Regression and Time series, Puzzles mostly repeating from previous years.

methodology used.

Q4: Question based on four different Time series data shown.

Final Interview (In person Round)
Finance Operations role 
Tell me about yourself. Basic questions on CV. Which project do you like most? Describe it. 
Situation: Algorithm does trading, so if one trade pair is such that it sells stock of a security like Reliance at say 
Rs. 100 in very large amount, this will create unrest in market and Reliance Bond prices will be lower, this 
algorithm will then buy these bonds to square off the position. This is called market manipulation and is not 
allowed. Questions are How will you detect this situation as there are million of trades its like needle in hay 
stock? What should you do to avoid this situation? Do you have any questions for us? 
Finance Research Role
Do you have clarity of roles or would you like us to explain? Question: 5 students marks in subjects are given. 2 
different students marks are not available in 2 different subjects. What is the best approximation? (Use KNN) Do 
you have any questions for us?
Additional Information
DE Shaw shortlists everyone. So prepare well. Going through last year internship experience and your projects , 
knowledge about finance trading are important. DE Shaw prefer CGPA, so have a good CGPA.

algorithm will then buy these bonds to square off the position. This is called market manipulation and is not 
allowed. Questions are How will you detect this situation as there are million of trades its like needle in hay 
stock? What should you do to avoid this situation? Do you have any questions for us?

different students marks are not available in 2 different subjects. What is the best approximation? (Use KNN) Do

rounds.content:
Round
1) The interview started of with questions about the competitions listed on the resume :
o Describe the dataset, what was the target variable, what kind of features did you create, What was the
model used and why was it better vs other alternatives. Then the discussion spanned off in different
directions based on the answers I was giving
o Define logistic regression what is the model form, when is it used, why is the link function, why is a log
present there?
2)
Then was asked questions on MLE, definition and how is it implemented .Batch Gradient Descent ,
SGD , Minbatch GD- why one is better than the other .
3)
Then went to Trees, Bagging vs Boosting, RF vs GBMs, GBMs vs XGBoost - What are the most
important differences amongst these algos. Splitting criterion, Regularization etc .
4)
Then he noticed the recommendation project I had showcased , started asking questions on
Collaborative Filtering , Item Based Recommenders - details and implementation in matrix
terminology.
5)
A simple SQL question around joins- just the pseudo code- Employee - Supervisor Then the next
10mins went around me asking him about his experience with Amazon etc.
75
Continued on next slide…
76
Additional Comments:
1)
Overall , all the ML topics listed in your resume will be thoroughly tested in detail. I wasn't asked 
to code , but a few of my friends were asked to.
2)
There were other ML concepts present in the resume around Graphs and Deep Learning - but 
weren't touched possibly in the interest of time and the comfort level of the interviewer. Hence I 
would recommend everyone to understand the math of all the ML algorithms and their 
implementation wherever possible. It is always recommended that you have diverse projects in 
terms of the data types ( tabular, image, text, graphs etc.), data sizes analyzed, etc. to standout .

feature embedding vector for n dictiory words. How does the Word2Vec

algorithms and alytics techniques that you will use in order to execute your

collinearity bewtween these features. What extra insight does this data

company records. What kind of biases our model might suffer from due to 
data problems? How can the missing data problem arise in this case?

Mostly Python, SQL and ML Theory based questions were asked in my PI.
1. Create a linear regression model pipeline from end to end (I was asked to 
share my screen, and show the virtual workflow on MS Word, explaining each 
step). I was also asked to write the pseudocode to create a python class for the 
same (something similar to AutoML)
2. Differentiate between Bagging and Boosting
3. Discussion on bias-variance trade-off in tree-based algorithms
4. Brief discussion on Adaboost, Gradboost, regularization terms in Xgboost 
and the need for regularization.
5. Overfitting in tree-based algorithms – factors related to overfitting in tree-
based algorithms?
6. Brief discussion on the need and the idea behind tree pruning.
7. Differentiate between a tuple and a list
8. What is the advantage of Pandas library w.r.t vectorised operations?
9. A fairly straightforward problem in SQL (Given a table D1 having attributes 
Emp_ID, Dept_ID, salary, write a query to select maximum salaries for each 
department)
10. For the same table, select the Emp_ID for which the maximum salary 
occurs as well (I wasn’t able to write the code on the spot, but I told the 
interviewer it could be done using nested queries)
11. Was asked a fairly straightforward coding problem (given a list of words, 
select only the words smaller than 5 letters using list comprehension in python)

3. Business case interview question: If you have the credit card data of each card user of India. How you 
would monetize this for Shaw. 
My Approach: As the dataset is huge, going to the individual level might not be useful so, I talked with 
them to understand what is relevant what is not. Finalised Transaction amount, source of transaction, 
recurring or not, type of purchase, POS, discounted or not etc. This will me to get the type of product 
segment is majorly purchased or is discount strategy for visa/mastercard/rupay is working or not, POS 
Walmart or Amazon etc. This will help Shaw to bet on which company to grow capital. At the end you 
have to improve the business of Shaw, so for that understand the business of Shaw well.
Continued on next slide…
Cont….
Conceptual questions were asked in between the case answering. Like I said I’ll be using multiple 
ANOVA. Follow Up questions were:
What is Multiple ANOVA. What are its components. How it is different from ANOVA. And what does 
each components signifies. What is AB testing and its initial hypothesis and alternate hypothesis etc.
Suggestions: Read Statistical Data Structures, Inference, Time Series, Regression and Case Studies 
with proper follow up questions. 
Aryan Chitransh
Continued on next slide…

Final Round (Offline Round) 40-45 Minutes:
•
She asked me to explain one of the projects in the CV. I have chosen my time series project 
which is stock price prediction. In this project we have used few models like ARIMA, ARIMAX 
and LSTM to forecast. 
•
How do we use ACF and PACF plots to determine the AR, MA components. 
•
What are the exogenous variables in the problem(I said GDP could be an exogenous, which has 
indirect effect on stock prices). 
•
Why did you use LSTM( I said, the predictions based on previous models were not good, to 
better know the structure behind and to have better predictions I have used LSTM. Unfortunately 
we were not able to get the correct AR and MA components that's one of other reasons as well to 
have used LSTM). 
•
Explain the architecture of LSTM( I have drawn and explained different gates and elaborated 
more on how does each gate is used to know the context). I went on for about 15-18 minutes 
including introduction. She straight away jumped onto the projects no questions about 
introduction
Continued on next slide…
Pelluru Manoj Sai Kumar

•

rounds.content:
Technical Round 1:
•
Interviewer asked to summarize the project on Topic Modelling (Unsupervised modelling) as the 
company was also working on a similar project as part of text analytics.
•
The follow up questions were what is NMF (Non Negative matrix Factorization) and what is Latent 
Dirichlet Allocation(LDA)? Why did you use only these particular models? Also asked basic questions 
on the metrics used.
Final Interview (40mins):
•
Interview started with my introduction, then the interviewer asked about the project on Topic 
Modelling which they are currently working on ( explained the same and he was good about that).
•
Then he gave me a case study about call centre ( utilization of call centre audio files) like how to 
leverage the audio transcript data to make business decisions. I came up with a couple of attributes 
which can be derived from them and explained him how a complete pipeline could be built. Then he 
asked about my PowerBI skills  and to rate my skills in PowerBI from 0-10. Asked about cloud 
experience.
•
TR mostly works on Media analytics which uses more text analytics and time series forecasting. So 
brush up deep learning techniques and forecasting part. Along with that there is a major use of 
PowerBI (dashboarding) and cloud(AWS). So any certifications related to cloud could be of great 
advantage.
•
Tips: Cloud certification and dashboarding skills are important.
Satyaki Sinha Ray 
Total Rounds:1 (AI Labs)
•
It was a coding+MCQ round, where I had to share screen to the interviewer while answering. 
Mostly ML related tech questions were asked in the MCQ section. For the coding part, we had to 
write only part of the code.
•
Once I was done with the coding part, he asked about NLP based questions like stemming, 
lemmatization. How does TF-IDF work? Basic questions on transformers and one question on 
basic working principles of CNN.

Vaishnav

Mayank Ray Mishra (offered)
Kindly share preparation strategy, material, topics etc. you feel is helpful. 
•
No GD involved
•
Resume shortlisting is black box - Since PGDBA doesn't suddenly make you a 10 + yrs 
experienced Data Scientist, most of the projects in everybody's resume is nearly the same. 
What matters is how you are able to formulate problem statement effectively, identify the 
problem that you were trying to solve, provide baseline solution and how you improved upon 
that & what was the business impact of your solution. Carefully articulating the words 
becomes important as it could be the HR/ technical person looking at the resume and that 
resume is the only means to judge a candidate at that moment. 
•
Make sure  if you have a target company which you are strongly feel aligned to (in terms of 
your professional aspirations), some project which can relate to what the company does can 
help you guide the interview in your favor. I did this by putting a healthcare domain additional 
project and  project in work-ex related to Pharma domain.

Lokesh Bhavsar (Offered)
•Total Rounds: 3

Technical Round 1 (Senior Project Manager) 45-50mins:
•
Introduce yourself, asked about what I learnt from the programme. Then asked about demand 
forecasting from WorkEx and overall profile, roles and responsibilities at Accenture.
•
General questions about course like mention two favourite subjects, what else did you learn apart 
from technical things?
•
Asked questions from NLP project, sentiment analysis, from business perspective. Follow up questions 
like what is word-to-vec and the business impact of R^2 value. What was the business problem? How 
did you convert it into data problem? For every project you need to have some interesting challenge.
•
I was asked on all the four projects, not very deep questions. I had to portray the business 
application of the project. The interviewer was not very technical person.
•
The interviewer was interested in stories of the projects like what’s the business problem and how did 
you convert it as data problem, what's the interesting part of the project? for every project motivation 
behind choosing the project. If you find the problem statement interesting then you need to be very 
clear on what interests you? Depending on company to company these questions may or may not be 
asked.
Continued…
•
Why do you want to join health care industry? Not just focus on tech things.
•
Be thoroughly prepared for the common 10-15 HR questions for all the companies.
•
Why this sector? We need to show ourselves that we are culturally fit for the company and be clear with 
our motivations for health care. 
•
My response was I have seen initiatives of Delhi govt in education sector. Education and health care are 
the two sectors to transform the society as these are part of the Maslow’s five fundamental human needs 
also Providence is a not for profit organization. If counter questions asked then try to answer based on 
the fundamental aspect of healthcare.

rounds.content:
Round 1: 
It was based on my submitted solution to the case study 
 
We had proposed a hybrid (content+collaborative) solution. Given the profile of customers, 
we would also do some clustering of customers, do market basket analysis, RFM analysis. 
Having implemented the solution, we could go for A/B testing. Since a large dataset was 
involved, I proposed an AWS based solution for implementing this solution. 
 
Their questions: "What's content and collaborative based recommender system, what's A/B 
testing?" 
 
They asked me about a classification project I had done on insurance claims fraud detection. 
They enquired about the exact business problem (An insurance company had received 
various automobile insurance claims and we had to predict whether those claims are 
fraudulent or not). They asked about various columns in the dataset, how I did data 
cleaning, feature engineering, how I addressed the imbalance in the data (they asked about 
SMOTE). They asked about the various models that I had used and finally about the 
performance metric (which was recall in this case).

Management ) 
 
He had submitted the Dns Case Study: Building a recommendation engine for a mobile application 
of ABC Bank, which will suggest to users different kinds of services provided by the bank. No dataset 
was given, and we were supposed to make a presentation explaining an approach 
 
My idea was to use two kinds of dataset : transaction data & customer profile data. My approach was 
to cluster customer profiles for a particular region, and then I would build a separate 
recommendation engine for each of these segments. I relied on K-means & DBScan for this 
clustering. Regarding customer profile, my chosen variables were : bank balance, credit score, age, 
monthly income, etc. For the transactions dataset, I relied on RFM (total transaction amount, 
monthly frequency, average amount of the transactions, etc. Once I had these customer segments, I 
proceeded to build the recommendation engine, which was built using RFM analysis, which I did 
for each user segment and product/service offered by the bank. Based on this information I found 
relative scores. I then adopted a collaborative filtering approach using these data ; customer 
segments, product/service and corresponding score I had calculated (scaled from 1-10). On the 
technical side, I build the recommendation engine using word-to-vec architecture, along with 
negative sampling and skip-gram model.

Round 2:  
 
~30-35 minutes. Given by an alumnus of Batch 1. 
 
This round was a bit more spicy. The 1st question he asked was "Tell me about an ML/DL algorithm 
that none of your batchmates know?" (I described how I used word2Vec arch to generate graph 
embeddings for a graph with negative sampling using skip-gram model, which I had used in my 
recommendation system project). He asked what my recommendation system project was about; 
what's collaborative filtering, why did I use collaborative filtering, what's meant my nearest 
neighbour graph, how do I construct it, What's the random walk that I've used here, the 2 models of 
Word2Vec architecture, what were my performance metrics (I had used intra-cluster similarity). He 
asked for an alternative approach/metric (I said OLS, he was okay with this). He asked "What's 
meant by eigenvalues and eigenvectors (in this context, he wanted to know a special property that 
when any matrix is multiplied by a vector, it performs a linear transformation involving shift, 
translation and rotation. Eigenvalues are those directions along which there's only scaling, no 
rotation). He asked "What's meant by PCA and SVD?" (PCA was mentioned in my CV and SVD is 
also kinda used in PCA, but this question was being asked to everyone by this panelist). He asked 
"What are the mathematical formulations for SVD & Eigenvalue decomposition as a special case of 
SVD; what's the relationship between SVD and PCA?" (If you look at the formula, SVD used a 
rectangular matrix. In such cases, you compute XTX and XXT, and you compute the correspond 
eigenvalues and eigenvectors for both; it so turns out that eigenvalues for both are same, 
theoretically. He was looking for the UsigmaV(t) formulation basically; in sklearn, after standard 
scaling the entire data, the mean vector becomes 0, so XTX represents nothing but matrix for 
covariance). He asked how my B.tech experience at Kgp was different from PGDBA experience. 
 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Technical Round (~15 minutes) 
It started with my introduction, where I mentioned few of my projects. However, I did not mention 
my recommender system project in my introduction, but they asked questions from it: "What's a 
recommender system, what different types of recommender system did you use, what was its 
ultimate objective?" 
 
Then they asked questions from my regression project. I explained my project. Then they asked 
"What's Regularisation? What is it used for? How is regularisation applied in the context of 
regression? Why is Lasso better that Ridge?" (I explained that regularisation is applied by adding one 
more term in the objective function which also have to be minimized; Lasso can be used for variable 
selection as few of the betas will go exactly to zero)

rounds.content:
52 
52 
credit score for each customer, vehicle age, total amount claimed, etc. I used K-means, 
spectral clustering, agglomerative clustering and DBSCAN to identify different clusters, and 
finally I stuck with K-means and spectral since they were giving almost similar results. I used 
the evaluation metric of Silhouette score and Davies-Bouldin index as performance metric 
(also WCSS score in case of k-means)). He asked what other categorical variables were there 
(but I didn't have any). Interviewer actually had a very good background in customer 
segmentation. There was a line in my CV about cluster profiling (done after completion of 
clustering). He asked "What exactly did you do in terms of profiling?" (My approach was to 
identify the distribution among claims, number of claims, total premium paid; since the best 
customer for an insurance company is one who pays all the premium and doesn't make any 
claim). He asked "How can you use this information?" (I found one of the 3 clusters to be 
very big, since this was a group of customers who had recently bought their vehicles, and had 
made minimum claims and had paid among the highest premiums. Distribution of vehicle 
age was also small. And for other 2 customers, vehicle age was old; hence I found customer's 
retention ratio was less). He asked a lot of questions on how I found all these things in detail. 
He asked then: "If a driver's score is added, how do you think that will influence things; what 
kind of distribution are you expecting in all 3 clusters identified?"    
 
He then literally put my CV aside and started asking questions: He asked about Pandas, 
PySpark, what exactly is a dataframe, how do you manipulate data, etc. He then gave me 2 
problems to perform data manipulation in Pandas, and then I had to perform the same 
manipulation in SQL (I used MySQL). He was more interested in the exact approach, 
however. I was given a question regarding students attendance dataset and the key was that 
he wanted me to use the CASE statement in SELECT statement, group by, having condition 
and where condition, and there was a non-equi (inequality) join too (2 tables). It was a long 
query, I had to explain the logic. Then I had to implement the same in Pandas.  
 
By another interviewer: "What exactly is meant by linear regression? What are its basic 
assumptions? What will happen if each of these assumptions is violated, and how would you 
rectify that? (I could answer these questions; Chapter 3 of ISLR basically)" 
 
HR questions: "Why do you wanna choose finance and not analytical consulting? Why do 
you think you are better than the rest?"

you still go for this approach? (Basic discussion was around bigrams and ngrams which 
capture the semantic meanings in the words. With them, I could use a count vectorizer, TF-
IDF, and other traditional models. However, hypothetically if everything could be fit in 
memory, there would be issues. Statements like "A eats pizza" and "Pizza eats A" would have

architecture? Why did you use accuracy and F-1 score as performance metrics?"

PCM. He conducted one test each for students A, B ,C , D & E for each of these subjects. 
He has marks of all 5 for physics and Chemistry but only 4 marks for Chemistry. Fill in this 
missing value." (My basic idea was to compare the marks, which were in the 90s, chemistry 
in 80s and Maths in 70s. Looking at the percentile values, the missing value had 4th rank in 
Physics and Maths so I took the average of 3rd and 5th guy's marks in Chemistry).

Technical Round 
 
Case Study was about a restaurant in Gurgaon. How would you forecast the revenue 
(making use of a list of exogenous variables), and which segments will be affected? My 
approach: First define your scope (what's the time period, revenue channels), then select 
your exogenous variables (variable categories should be MECE, macro level factors should 
be pre -thought. In my case, covid related government restrictions/incentives were 
considered by me; then ask for their thoughts & suggestion on your variables). Every point 
should be backed by logical reasoning.  
 
Other questions: Why do we have a Harmonic mean for F1 score? Basic Macro questions 
(Economics: BDM  & FRM course should be done before holidays) - GDP, recession, 
monetary policies. Python queries related to data manipulation - mostly Pandas NumPypy 
: How do you rate yourself on a scale of 1-10 in python and SQL (rated 8 and 5 respectively): 
dataset has these columns, and how do you extract a certain output 
 
I would rate this round Moderate to Difficult

rounds.content:
HR Round. They asked: “If we roll out the offer, will you accept it?” 
 
 
My overall experience was Excellent, one of the best interview experiences. Know 
everything about how Shaw operates. Have good hold on Regression & Time series.  I had 
pre prepared my mindset before the interview. I used to think a lot about exogenous variables 
and how I would monetise them. PPT skills are very important ( need to prepare a decent 
one quickly) 
 
Rohan’s Preparation Strategy: Started preparing while creating the CV. Projects are most 
important. 50% prep was done with CV prep. Next, identified broad topics (regression, time 
series, deep, etc.). Studies regression from ISLR (2 & 3) and Montgomery book, time series 
(SPA link) focused on practical learning via projects wrt time series. ML models from ISLR 
and statquest videos (thoroughly) and IIM C (Business Data Mining course), Deep Learning 
IIT KGP (Sudeshna Sarkar slides (topics only) and Mitesh Khapra YT videos, and IIT KGP 
book is also good). Didn't attend deep learning classes in KGP (prof taught that poorly), 
Kaggle project is imp.  
 
Inference is most important for statistics. Studied mostly in ISI semester. Imp are CI, Hypo 
testing, A/B testing, p-interval, power of Test (we could be asked to design our own 
hypothesis in interviews : null, alt, etc.)

provide ranking on features with their positive and negative impact on our target variable, and they 
also give information about the design space. They are used above the ML models).

had different compounds (their formula, indicating elements and bonds) and we had to predict 
whether these molecules were inhibiting the HIV virus or not. We visualized elements as nodes, and 
bonds connecting them as edges, and approach this as a graph neural network problem. We could 
utilize a transformer kind of algorithm to solve this problem. They asked how attention would be 
used for this graph neural network. The discussion went deep into graph neural networks. I gave an 
answer accordingly, but they weren't particularly satisfied with it. (Last year they had not asked these 
questions, so this was a complete surprise!) 
 
They also asked some questions on python related to string reversal (I could do that; can't recall the

1. He directly began with a graph problem, where we are given traffic congestion data for different 
time points for different nodes. How will you optimize the traffic flow? I came up with some 
approach but he wasn't satisfied. 
 
2.  He gave another graph problem where using age, weight, height, BMI we need to predict some 
output and the features have a causal structure. How will you utilize this causal structure for 
prediction? Since the features are linked the edge weights could be the correlation strength between 
the two and this would imply that we might have multicollinearity issues. We may have to use PCA 
to decorrelate the features. He asked to explain PCA and why eigenvectors are orthonormal. He was 
ok with the approach but more importantly he wanted me to approach it using Bayesian inference 
(I later asked him about the approach) 
 
3. He saw my DL project and asked to explain it, how fine tuning was done. Then he gave a problem, 
we are given patient notes and we need to build a model which will be able to answer general 
questions about the prescription of a patient.

BCG interviews weren't pressure interviews as such. They were directing us as and when needed. 
They wanted to check whether we can answer all questions or not and if not, are we able to pick up 
their nudges and move in the right direction 
 
Monal’s Preparation Strategy: I started preparing 1.5 months before the placements. I started 
with  business case studies (from IIM A book). Then I moved into ML concepts (read ISLR twice). 
I focused on Deep Learning (as I was interested in AI Garage).  I brushed up on ML concepts. I did 
the bare minimum wrt classes this time.  
 
Materials for case questions: IIM A case book, IIM Lucknow's channels, BCG Gamma online case 
studies. 
 
Materials for ML concepts : Course slides, ISLR, medium (mostly for Deep Learning), spark by 
examples website (for Big Data), For doubts : Gooldfellow's book and Youtube channels (statquest, 
Zed statistics, jbstatistics, ritwik maths). I found UDK rather superficial.  
 
Towards the end, I used to pick one algo from my resume and think in what different ways it could 
fail and how I could address that 
 
Important subjects : CDS, Inference, SPA (for initial rounds and puzzles), Deep Learning, Big Data 
(if you have taken the elective and mentioned so in your resume), basic idea of algorithms 
 
General tips : Start with the ML concepts from your CV. For the projects mentioned on your 
resume, be thorough with all concepts, which other models can be used for similar problem 
statements, what are the current flaws in your problem and how you can improve it.

~30 minutes. Business Case Round: There's a hotel chain in Sydney, and they are struggling to 
meet their profit targets and their profits are declining since the last few months. They have hired 
you. Analyze the situation (very open ended). 
 
I started by asking questions: Is this a revenue side or cost side problem, are they paying more (than 
industry standards) to their employees, are the raw material costs going up, etc on the cost side and 
what are the different revenue channels for the hotel. Interviewer then mentioned that it's a revenue

source: room charges, 2nd channel is restaurant (I was thinking out loud, interviewer was nudging 
in preferred directions). Interviewer then asked how would you collect data (from whom) for each 
of these revenue channels. Then he asked how would you quantify these revenue channels. [X 
number of rooms, avg cost and occupancy of each room; I answered likewise for all channels]. I

answered that this wasn't an issue, as customers could choose the pharmacy. Then I started asking 
questions that would help me profile the customers who don't show up (maybe young people aren't 
very serious wrt taking medicines). They asked what factors besides age could affect a patient's 
decision to buy medicines. I answered if a customer is regularly visiting the doctor, we'll probably 
have past medical history of that patient, through which we can see for what kind of diseases people 
usually buy medicines for. Then they asked "Suppose you can do this kind of profiling and predict 
whether a customer will buy a certain medicine or not. What will you do thereafter?" I answered that 
if our model predicts that customer is not going to show up, we need not keep those medicines 
packed." Then they countered: "What if the customer actually shows up contrary to the model's 
prediction? What will you do?" I answered that this is a supply chain issue, a kind of back-ordering. 
Companies regularly deal with such issues. Then the interviewer asked "Can you think of some other 
way in which you can promote the sale of medicines?" I answered: "Apollo Pharmacy has its mobile 
app. We can send reminders (notification/nudges) to customers to buy the medicines. We can share 
articles/information about the negative effects of the disease(s) the customer is facing, and how 
important taking that medicine is." Interviewer was satisfied with this answer and the case ended 
here. 
 
Then he again asked those questions around “Why did you leave your job?” and the interview ended 
there.
